failure_prevention.root_cause: The runner used git ls-files with an intentional error-on-miss mode to prove android/key.properties was untracked. The expected healthy miss wrote native stderr; Windows PowerShell 5.1 with ErrorActionPreference Stop promoted that stderr into NativeCommandError before the runner could interpret LASTEXITCODE.
failure_prevention.permanent_rule: Never intentionally provoke native stderr/nonzero exit to prove an expected-negative Git condition in Windows PowerShell 5.1. Use a non-erroring query and inspect returned data.
failure_prevention.replacement_strategy: git ls-files -- <path> then exact membership test

failure_prevention.root_cause: The first regression gate searched the entire PowerShell source for a forbidden token. The historical explanation comment intentionally contained that token, so CI rejected the repaired runner even though the executable Git command was already safe.
failure_prevention.permanent_rule: Regression checks for dangerous native-command forms must be command-aware and must not classify comments or documentation as executable behavior.
failure_prevention.replacement_strategy: Inspect executable-looking git ls-files invocation lines and separately assert the safe membership-query form.

failure_prevention.root_cause: The runner resolved Windows-only external signing authority paths from USERPROFILE before the platform-neutral ValidateOnly early exit. On Linux CI, USERPROFILE was null, so ValidateOnly failed before validation could complete.
failure_prevention.permanent_rule: Validate-only paths must not touch platform-specific environment variables, secret stores, keystore locations, or execution-only filesystem state. Bind those values only after ValidateOnly exits and after the Windows platform guard.
failure_prevention.replacement_strategy: Execute -ValidateOnly on non-Windows CI and require USERPROFILE-based external signing authority binding to occur after the ValidateOnly exit.
